claims.claim: חברות הבינה המלאכותית הוציאו 56 מיליון דולר על 'לובי שקט' (בכותרת המלאה לפי אינדקס החיפוש: 'בבחירות האמצע')
claims.verified_figure: $55.7M spent so far (as of ~2026-09-30) on the 2026 US midterms by super PACs aligned with OpenAI (Leading the Future network) and Anthropic (Public First Action network), per a New York Times tally; $52.6M of it in safe seats, almost all in primaries.
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: 56 מיליון דולר; search snippet of the article describes AI companies using political committees to fund candidates of both parties while blurring the link to the companies' agenda, citing an NYT investigation into Anthropic and OpenAI backing of dozens of candidates.
claims.note: $56M is a fair rounding of the NYT's $55.7M, and the time frame (2026 midterm cycle to date) matches. The figure is NOT federal lobbying spending under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; it is super PAC election spending, and the full article title says 'בבחירות האמצע'. 'לובי' is used loosely, and the homepage-truncated headline drops the midterms qualifier. Attribution caveat: the money comes from super PACs 'aligned with' the companies, not from company treasuries alone. Public First is reportedly funded with at least $20M from Anthropic, while Leading the Future is largely funded by individuals (Andreessen, Horowitz, Greg Brockman), so 'of the AI companies' simplifies things. Neither caveat changes the number. Article body unreadable (EGRESS_BLOCKED), and the NYT original was not fetched directly; the figure was confirmed through multiple consistent secondary reports.
